finding.claim: Client-controlled Connection header lets an unauthenticated downstream client strip any header from the upstream request, including headers the proxy's own filters injected (e.g. forwarding/identity headers). Severity: low-medium, depends on what backends trust.
finding.source: Downstream HTTP/1.1 or h2 request header `Connection: <name>` (any listed token, any client, no auth).
finding.sink: Removal of request headers in upstream_request_filter, after filter-injected headers were already written to the session.

trace.note: Filter-set headers (headers_to_set) are inserted into the session request header during request_filter.
Filter extra_request_headers (promoted headers) are also inserted into the session request header.
upstream_request_filter calls strip_hop_by_hop after the pipeline has run; no_body.rs:183 is identical.
strip_hop_by_hop calls strip_connection_tokens with the client's Connection values, snapshotted at line 35.
Splits each Connection value on ',' and trims tokens.
Only tokens in the static REQUEST_HOP_BY_HOP list are skipped; any other name, including filter-injected ones, is removed.
remove_header_by_name deletes the header from the upstream request.

finding.guards_checked: validation.rs:30-44 (Host checks) and normalize.rs:59-67 (duplicate CL/CT, obs-fold) do not inspect Connection. reserved_headers only rejects x-praxis-*/x-ext-* names. The static list (hop_by_hop.rs:24-33) does not include application headers. No allowlist of removable names exists. Upstream strip runs after the filters write their headers. Not verified: whether the backends in a real deployment rely on the injected headers.
finding.repro: Configure a filter that injects X-Authenticated-User after auth. Send `GET /x HTTP/1.1`, `Host: a`, `Connection: X-Authenticated-User`. The upstream receives the request without X-Authenticated-User. Use a trust-on-absence backend to see the impact.

finding.claim: Connection-listed Content-Length is removed from the upstream request while the body is still forwarded. This may cause request-body framing desync (request smuggling) on reused upstream keep-alive connections. CANDIDATE: needs verification against the pingora-core version in use, because its upstream framing logic is not in this repo.
finding.source: Downstream request with a body and `Content-Length: N` plus `Connection: content-length`.
finding.sink: Upstream HTTP/1.1 request sent by Pingora with no Content-Length and no Transfer-Encoding, but with body bytes still forwarded. Upstream keep-alive reuse then treats the body as the next request.

trace.note: Connection values are split into tokens.
`content-length` is not in REQUEST_HOP_BY_HOP, so it is treated as a removable token.
Content-Length is removed from the upstream request header.
strip_hop_by_hop applies this on every request, with no check that framing headers are kept.
apply_mutated_content_length only restores CL in StreamBuffer mode with a body writer. Nothing restores it otherwise.
Pingora forwards the body after the filtered header is written; no re-framing in this repo.

finding.guards_checked: validation.rs and normalize.rs check duplicate CL and obs-fold on CL only. No check rejects or restores framing headers after strip_hop_by_hop. No TE+CL conflict check exists in this repo (see below). Unverified: whether pingora-core re-derives body framing from downstream state, which would make this non-exploitable. Pingora source is not present under ~/.cargo/registry.
finding.repro: POST /x HTTP/1.1, `Host: a`, `Content-Length: 11`, `Connection: content-length`, body `GET /admin HTTP/1.1` against a keep-alive upstream. Check whether the upstream sees a second request. The upstream must be pingora-proxied and keep-alive reuse must be enabled.

finding.claim: The admin listener serves unauthenticated KV read, write, delete and list on /api/kv/*, with no auth or loopback check in code. Anyone who can reach admin_addr can read and modify the KV stores that filters consult. Severity: medium, conditional on the admin_addr binding (set in config, not in this repo).
finding.source: Any TCP client that can reach the admin listener: PUT/DELETE/GET /api/kv/{store}/{key}, GET /api/kv/{store}.
finding.sink: KvStoreRegistry backend writes and deletes, which filters read through TcpFilterContext.kv_stores and HttpFilterContext.kv_stores.

trace.note: add_admin_endpoints_to_pingora_server takes admin_addr from config with no loopback or auth requirement.
service.add_tcp(admin_addr) binds the listener to the configured address.
PingoraAdminService::response dispatches any /api/kv/ path to dispatch_kv_request with no authentication check.
dispatch_kv_request routes by method and path with no caller identity.
handle_set writes to the store with no authorization.
handle_delete removes keys with no authorization.
handle_list dumps all entries in a store.
kv_stores from the pipeline is passed into every filter context, so writes via admin are visible to filters.

finding.guards_checked: read_body caps request bodies at 1 MiB (kv/mod.rs:25, 129-132). Store capacity returns 507 (kv/mod.rs:176). JSON escaping of keys and values is correct (service.rs:36-54, kv/mod.rs:159-161, 202-209). Route parsing is sound (kv/mod.rs:92-107). None of these is an authentication or authorization control. The deprecated PingoraKvService (kv/mod.rs:110) has the same gap. The admin bind address and any network policy are not in this repo, so exposure cannot be confirmed.
finding.repro: If admin_addr is reachable: `curl -X PUT --data 'allow' http://<admin>/api/kv/<store>/<key>` succeeds with no credentials. `curl http://<admin>/api/kv/<store>` lists every entry.
